back: The change in direction of light passing at an angle from one medium into another, caused by a change in speed.

front: Which way does light bend at a boundary?
back: Into a denser medium: slows, bends towards the normal. Into a less dense medium: speeds up, bends away.
$n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \dfrac{\text{speed in vacuum}}{\text{speed in medium}}$
The incident ray, refracted ray and normal lie in one plane; sin i / sin r is constant for two given media.

front: A ray along the normal at a boundary?
back: It passes straight through without changing direction (but changes speed).
Water looks shallower than it is because light from the bottom bends away from the normal as it leaves the water.

front: A ray through a parallel-sided glass block?
back: It emerges parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways.
